findings.reason: At base 1b75b3376bbaca6bf692a0a341d4f8085e43063b, items 119, 130, 146 and 47 and the report overview do not consistently propagate accepted sourceIssues E34/E44. Independently checked the three displayed equations: their discriminants are t^10, t^11 and t^8(t^2+t+1); Tate's original algorithm, pp.47-51, gives split I2*, I3* and IV* at zero and nonsplit I2, I1 and I2 at infinity; their rational-fibre point sums are 25. Read v3 pp.28-33, 37-38 and 49: the elliptic table comes from Theorem 10.4, and the IV* exclusion uses an additional multiple fibre of type III or IV, which does not cover the new E4 case. Correct fix: make the classification-dependent items explicitly conditional on a missing exclusion/completeness gate and propagate that gate to both endpoints and the overview. Preserve the main theorem as a target. These Jacobians are not Enriques counterexamples. I did not independently reproduce the earlier exhaustive fourteen-class computation, so simply declaring a corrected table exhaustive is not a verified repair; retain that computation's separate completeness obligation.

The missing dependencies are real: v3 Proposition 8.1, p.22, invokes EGA IV4 18.5.11, Raynaud 8.2.1, a dominating normal model and Lemma 8.4, while item 81 and route 2 do not expose those proof leaves. The proposed EGA statement is wrong as an attribution: the actual theorem, printed pp.130-131, characterises henselian local rings, including the finite local component of a separated locally finite-type morphism quasi-finite at a closed-fibre point. It is not the claimed general Cartier-divisor-lifting theorem. Import that exact henselian result and separately plan the regular relative-curve transverse-divisor/finite-DVR adapter used here. Raynaud's theorem, printed p.66, is for proper flat relative curves over a trait satisfying (N)*; a section gives a degree-one generic divisor, so (ii)->(iii)->(iv) supplies cohomological flatness. Record the no-embedded-special-fibre condition, normality at its maximal points and f_*O_X=O_S from 6.1.4, or prove them using the normal model. h1=1 additionally uses the genus-one Euler characteristic. Request general suppliers from SchemeAndStackFoundations/coherent-cohomology owners; route only their application and model-comparison leaves to the genus-one continuation.
